findings.evidence: Fiber.lean:93-96; it is the only declaration in the file whose statement depends on `open scoped Classical`. `grep -rn occCount_of_injective code/` matches only Fiber.lean (definition and docstring line 22), so no consumer currently pins the classical form.
findings.fix: Drop `open scoped Classical in` and take `[Decidable (∃ x, f x = y)]` as an instance argument (or state it as `occCount f y = if y ∈ Set.range f then 1 else 0` with `[Decidable (y ∈ Set.range f)]`). Alternatively delete it: both branches are already available as `occCount_eq_one` (line 105) and `occCount_eq_zero` (line 86), and nothing in the repository uses it.
findings.issue: `occCount_of_injective`'s `if ∃ x, f x = y then 1 else 0` is decidable only through the file-local `open scoped Classical in` (line 93), so the statement bakes in `Classical.propDecidable`. A consumer's goal carrying a concrete `Decidable (∃ x, f x = y)` instance is not reducibly defeq to it, so `rw [occCount_of_injective]` fails there — and the author's reply keeps this lemma precisely as "an explicit rewriting theorem".

findings.evidence: TransitionCount.lean:90-92 proves it by `rw [occCount_eq_sum, occCount_eq_sum, Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]; rfl`; lines 108-110 likewise with `Fin.sum_univ_succ`. The same argument moved `occCount_eq_sum`, `occCount_le_of_comp` and `occCount_lt_of_comp` into `Function` in this PR (Fiber.lean:50,55,63); these two are the unmoved remainder of the same set.
findings.fix: Move both into `namespace Function` alongside `occCount` (in `TauCeti/Data/Fintype/Fiber.lean`, adding `public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin`, or in a `Fin`-indexed companion file), and update the uses in `TauCeti/Combinatorics/Enumerative/SuccessorArray.lean:189,226` and the `open Function (...)` lists.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.occCount_comp_castSucc_add_last` (line 89) and `TauCeti.occCount_comp_succ_add_zero` (line 107) are general lemmas about `Function.occCount` — their statements mention only `Fin`, a bare `α` and `occCount`, and their proofs contain no word or transition content — yet they stay public in `namespace TauCeti` in the word file while the rest of the `occCount` API moved to `Function`. A user of `Function.occCount` finds its splitting lemmas under `TauCeti.occCount_*`, in a module about transition counts.

summary: The relocation itself is clean — old names fully deleted, bodies hidden behind `occCount_def := (rfl)`, regrouping and sum lemmas now in usable general form. Two surface defects remain: `occCount_of_injective` states its `ite` with `Classical.propDecidable`, and two general `Function.occCount` lemmas stayed in the `TauCeti` namespace, splitting the API across two namespaces.
